## Historical audit: S0035

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2/results/r1/fixed_h0/H0/development/commons_129095630/trajectory.jsonl`. Only supplied chunk 2 is visible. Line 12 is a complete observation at characters [0,183493); lines 13–16 are complete observations, with their respective full ranges cited below.

| Evidence | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| Goal and scene, line 12, student `model_request`, [0,183493) | The stated task was to reconstruct a 512 × 384 indoor photograph as separate meshes, matching camera and framing. The student’s code interpreted it as a toolmaker’s workshop: multiple benches, drawers, tools, cans, a stool and an organizer. Those labels are the student’s interpretation, not independent identification of the unseen image. |
| Construction and repair, line 12 | The programs specified separate primitive parts, positioned drawer components and tool hinges, procedural noise and bump materials, a camera and area lights. Step 1 failed because the Blender world was `None`. The revised program created a world when absent; step 2 returned `ok: true` and logged a saved render and blend file. This validates execution, not visual fidelity or part connections. |
| Review and revision, lines 12–15: line 13 `codex_session` [0,3337), line 14 student `model_response` [0,16177), line 15 `execute` [0,16817) | The next student session was supplied the reference and step-2 render; its internal visual assessment is not shown. It returned and executed a complete revision, including unique object names, darker materials, more detail, a shifted stool, changed camera and lighting, and color-preservation logic. These are observed edits, not proof that they improved the match. The session recorded zero tool calls; no separate autonomous search is visible. |
| Final execution, line 16 `execution_result` [0,1078) | Step 3 timed out after approximately 576 seconds, with empty stdout/stderr and no image. The cause is not established. This is a technical interruption, not an empty patch or demonstrated algorithmic failure. Step 2 is the last visibly successful build; the final submission outcome is not shown. |

**Teacher input:** No teacher message, detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or adoption is visible in this chunk. The runtime’s error and comparison prompt were received, and the subsequent world-handling change addresses that error; they should not be attributed to a teacher.

**Lessons and uncertainty:** The transferable observation is that a concrete runtime exception was followed by a targeted repair and a successful render; successful execution alone cannot establish scene accuracy. The workshop objects, textures, poses and camera choices are task-specific hypotheses. Neither image is visible to this audit, so object presence, material appearance, actual contact or intersections, pose, framing and lighting quality remain unverified. The timeout’s relationship to scene complexity is also unresolved. No formal reconstruction score or final correctness determination is visible.
